Consider the following mathematical expression:

\[ {@expr@} \]

Determine whether this number is rational or irrational.

Your answer: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

We are asked to classify the expression:

\[ \sqrt{{@n@}} \]

A number is rational if it can be written as a fraction of two integers \(\frac{a}{b}\). Square roots of positive integers are rational only if the integer under the root is a perfect square.

In this case, {@n@} is {@if type_choice = 0 then "a perfect square." else "not a perfect square."@}

{@if type_choice = 0 then sconcat("

\\[ \\sqrt{", n, "} = ", sqrt(n), " \\]

") else ""@}

{@explanation@}

Therefore, the correct classification is {@correct_ans@}.
